# nvs / phy_init are unchanged from the stock single-app layout on purpose:
# nvs holds the bonded-device link keys the sticky-reconnect path depends on
# leaving its offset and size alone means an existing unit keeps its pairings
# across this repartition. Growing nvs would push phy_init off 0xf000 and force
# the first app slot off the 64K boundary it needs.
# ota_0 sits exactly where 'factory' used to. There is deliberately no factory
# slot: with otadata blank the bootloader boots ota_0

# Omnitone partition table - ESP32-PICO-: # subtype is just a value the CSV parser accepts for a data partition; nothing
# mounts it. Reads go through esp_partition_read() against
# esp_partition_find_first(ESP_PARTITION_TYPE_DATA
# ESP_PARTITION_SUBTYPE_DATA_SPIFFS
8MB embedded flash: "audio"). A firmware OTA does not touch it.

# Omnitone partition table - ESP32-PICO-: # otadata: the bootloader's record of which slot is active and whether the
# running image has been confirmed (CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE). It
# cannot go in the 0x9000..0x10000 gap because nvs+phy_init already fill it
# it lands after audio. App slots must start on a 0x10000 boundary
# starts at 0x420000 rather than immediately after the 8K otadata.
# log: 1M of raw flash for the runtime log (flog.c)
# the nRF pulls over the bridge with LOG_INFO / LOG_READ. Like audio it is NOT
# a filesystem - a filesystem would erase sectors on its own schedule
# the ESP32 an erase stalls both cores long enough to punch a hole in the
# audio. flog only erases when the output is idle. Type 0x40 is the first
# user-defined type; the audio partition predates that convention.
# coredump: reserved now so enabling CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_ENABLE_TO_FLASH later
# is an sdkconfig change and not another serial reflash. Nothing writes it yet.
# Ends at 0x730000
